A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on conversational inertia, Context Preference Learning (CPL), and Clip Context. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the relocated attention visualizations.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations across eight environments, BrowseComp experiments, general-capability evaluations, attention analyses, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, model-specific inertia measurements, and a Qwen3-1.7B CPL evaluation.

M1.justification: CPL retains the same preference-pair construction, filtering, short-context DPO objective, and LoRA training procedure. Clip Context retains the same periodic history-clearing mechanism. Applying CPL to Qwen3-1.7B and combining Clip with a retrieval baseline do not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: The eight agent environments, BrowseComp, GPQA-Diamond, and MMLU-Redux are retained. The added comparisons and analyses use existing environments; the smaller-model experiment changes model configuration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix P adds evaluated comparisons against StreamingLLM and SeCoM paired with Window and Clip (Tables 11–12). These introduce token-level streaming and retrieval-based comparators beyond v1's Long, Window, and Summarization comparisons.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a 2,048-token StreamingLLM configuration, an average-input-length control for SeCoM, and Qwen3-1.7B training with Qwen3-8B preference data followed by Window-6 evaluation. Table 13 also introduces repeat-last-action measurements. The original evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix Q adds distinct tests of model-dependent inertia and preference-data transfer: Qwen3-8B versus Llama3.1-8B attention/repetition diagnostics, and transfer from Qwen3-8B preference data to Qwen3-1.7B. Appendix M also expands hyperparameter sensitivity evidence with per-environment results. The earlier ablations and failure-case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The SEM procedures in Appendices H and J and the existing repeated-run disclosures are unchanged. Tables 10–14 add no new uncertainty estimates, significance tests, seed information, or explicit increases in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 10–14 add substantial results while Tables 1–9 remain unchanged. New comparisons report StreamingLLM averaging 54.6 versus Clip's 68.9, and Qwen3-1.7B averaging 50.9 before CPL versus 52.7 after CPL. Reporting inconsistencies remain: Table 10 gives Clip-12to1 an average of 69.2 versus 68.9 in retained Table 1, while Table 12's Clip-12to1 row reproduces Table 10's Clip-12to3 values. These discrepancies do not establish verified same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The DPO objective, context-trimming equation, LoRA formulation, and Appendix F computational-complexity derivation are retained. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical revisions appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: identifying conversational inertia, mitigating it with reward-free CPL and Clip Context, and improving agent performance and efficiency. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendices P–Q add explanations involving preserved interaction boundaries, retrieval-query quality, and stronger baseline inertia as reasons for performance differences. Section 5 makes limitations more explicit, including excluding reward sparsity from scope. Information-loss failures and the underlying tradeoff were already discussed in v1's Appendix L.

D1.justification: v3 documents four sink tokens and a 2,048-token context for StreamingLLM, retrieval of two historical observation–action pairs for SeCoM, and the data source and evaluation context for Qwen3-1.7B. Existing training, hardware, environment, and prompt details are retained; no new code or data release is announced.

R1.justification: v3 adds StreamingLLM and SeCoM citations and a Section 4 paragraph positioning the approach against sliding-window, summarization, and retrieval methods. The central novelty positioning remains stable. Numerous other reference edits concern bibliographic metadata rather than new research relationships.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization remain intact. Changes include a related-work paragraph, an explicit limitations block, expanded Appendix M, new Appendices P–Q, reference cleanup, and removal of the stray 'General Response 3' reference. The former visualization Appendix P becomes Appendix R.

P2.justification: v3 adds five compact appendix tables using the existing presentation style and regroups the retained attention heatmaps under Appendix R. Existing figures and table designs are preserved, with limited reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful comparative and diagnostic evidence absent in v1, particularly the StreamingLLM comparison, model-specific inertia analysis, and within-family transfer to Qwen3-1.7B. Applicability limits are also more visible. These gains are moderated by conflicting scores between Tables 1 and 10 and the ambiguous Clip configuration in Table 12, which weaken confidence in part of the added evidence.
